- When sentiment is negative (especially > -0.5) and forecast is rising, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% to avoid overcorrection.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+2.0% from prior day), cap forecast increase to avoid overshoot; allow 1–2 days of lag before full momentum is captured.
- If sentiment turns positive (e.g., >0.1) and forecast is flat or falling, increase forecast by 0.5–1.0% to capture sentiment-driven rebound.
- Mean-reversion bias: if forecast is >+1.5% above recent 5-day average, reduce by 0.3–0.7% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day horizon, avoid overfitting to recent 7–14 day highs; use 30-day moving average as baseline anchor for correction.
- If sentiment is consistently negative over 3–5 days, suppress forecast momentum; treat as “bearish baseline” with 0.5–1.0% downward bias.
